title: Three people in one team locked out inside an hour

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: Three of us locked out this morning

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
Three people in my team have been locked out since about half eight - me, Sara
and Joe. Different laptops, different floors, and Joe has been off all week so
he has not touched anything.

None of us has changed a password recently.

Mel

handling.escalation_reason: Lockouts affecting several people at once are treated as a possible password-spray attempt and go to security.

rationale: The lockout runbook is retrieved, is the right runbook, and its 'When to escalate' section is the whole answer: more than one person locked out at once is a possible password-spray attempt and goes to security rather than to the desk (G6). Joe having been away all week is the detail that rules out the cached-credential explanation that makes case-056 routine. Security-sensitive under G3, which forces at least P2; a reviewer who reads three blocked people plus a suspected attack as P1 has a case, and the difference matters because P1 routes to oncall.
